name: Hoshea
overview: The name Hoshea, also spelled Oshea, originally belonged to Joshua, the son of Nun from the tribe of Ephraim, who was renamed Jehoshua by Moses as he led Israel (Numbers 13:8,16; Deuteronomy 32:44). This name later identifies a king of Israel who rose to power by assassinating Pekah, but his reign was marked by evil, submission to Assyria, and eventual imprisonment due to conspiracy (subtopics). The history of Hoshea as king reflects a period when Israel feared neither the Lord nor their king, leading to national instability and judgment, as hinted in Hosea 10:3 and 10:7. Additionally, Hoshea appears among Jewish exiles, underscoring the consequences of Israel’s disobedience.
